1.title: The Rule of Three
1.content: Limit your outfit to three main colours maximum. This creates visual harmony and prevents your look from appearing chaotic or overwhelming.

2.title: Dress for Your Colour Season
2.content: Wearing colours that complement your natural colouring (skin tone, hair, eyes) makes you look healthier and more vibrant. Discover whether you're a Spring, Summer, Autumn, or Winter.

3.title: Neutral Foundation, Colour Accent
3.content: Build outfits on neutral foundations (black, white, grey, navy, beige) and introduce colour through accessories or one statement piece.

4.title: Understanding Warm vs Cool Tones
4.content: Warm undertones pair beautifully with earthy colours (olive, mustard, coral), while cool undertones shine in jewel tones (emerald, sapphire, ruby). Knowing yours transforms your shopping.

5.title: The Power of Monochrome
5.content: Dressing in one colour family creates an elongating, sophisticated effect. Vary shades and textures within the same hue for depth and interest.

6.title: Complementary Colour Mastery
6.content: Colours opposite on the colour wheel (blue/orange, purple/yellow, red/green) create striking, dynamic outfits when balanced properly.

7.title: Navy is the New Black
7.content: Navy is universally flattering and pairs beautifully with more colours than black. It's softer, more approachable, and equally versatile.

8.title: White Brightens Your Face
8.content: Wearing white or cream near your face reflects light upward, making you look more awake and vibrant. Ideal for video calls and photographs.

9.title: Pattern Mixing with Colour
9.content: When mixing patterns, ensure they share at least one common colour. This creates cohesion even with different scales and styles of print.

10.title: The 60-30-10 Colour Rule
10.content: Use your dominant colour for 60% of your outfit, secondary colour for 30%, and accent colour for 10%. This creates balanced, visually pleasing looks.

11.title: Seasonal Colour Rotation
11.content: Rotate your colour palette with seasons: rich jewel tones for autumn/winter, soft pastels and brights for spring/summer. This keeps your wardrobe feeling fresh.

12.title: Black from Head to Toe
12.content: All-black outfits are timeless and slimming but require texture variation (matte, shine, knit) to avoid looking flat or costume-like.

13.title: Colour Blocking Basics
13.content: Colour blocking uses blocks of solid, contrasting colours for bold impact. Keep silhouettes simple and let the colours do the talking.

14.title: Metallic as a Neutral
14.content: Gold and silver metallics work as neutrals and can be paired with almost any colour. Match metallics to your undertone for the most flattering effect.

15.title: Print Scale Matters
15.content: Choose print sizes that work with your frame - smaller frames suit smaller prints, larger frames can carry bolder patterns without being overwhelmed.

16.title: The Third Piece Rule
16.content: Elevate any outfit by adding a third piece - a blazer, cardigan, scarf, or structured bag. This transforms basic combinations into complete, intentional looks.

17.title: Proportion Play
17.content: Balance volume in your outfit: if wearing something loose on top, go fitted on bottom (and vice versa). This creates flattering silhouettes on all body types.

18.title: The One-Statement Rule
18.content: Let one piece be the star of your outfit. If wearing a bold pattern or statement accessory, keep everything else understated to avoid visual competition.

19.title: Define Your Waist
19.content: Creating definition at your natural waist, whether through belts, tucking, or tailored cuts, creates an hourglass silhouette that flatters most body types.

20.title: The Rule of Thirds
20.content: Instead of dividing your body in half, aim for a 1/3 to 2/3 ratio (short top with high-waisted bottoms, or longer top with shorter skirt) for more dynamic proportions.

21.title: Vertical Lines Elongate
21.content: Vertical stripes, long necklaces, and open cardigans create the illusion of height and a leaner silhouette. Use strategically for lengthening effects.

22.title: V-Necks Flatter Everyone
22.content: V-necklines elongate the neck, draw the eye vertically, and flatter virtually every face shape and body type. A universally flattering choice.

23.title: The Power of High-Waisted
23.content: High-waisted bottoms visually lengthen legs and create a longer, leaner silhouette. They work particularly well when tops are tucked in.

24.title: Structured vs Unstructured Balance
24.content: Pair structured pieces (blazers, tailored trousers) with softer items (silk blouses, knit tops) for outfits that feel polished yet approachable.

25.title: Layering Without Bulk
25.content: Layer thin, quality fabrics rather than thick ones. Start with fitted base layers and add progressively looser pieces to avoid adding unnecessary volume.

26.title: The Half-Tuck
26.content: A casual half-tuck (tucking just the front of your shirt) creates waist definition while maintaining a relaxed, effortless vibe. Perfect for casual elegance.

27.title: Dress for Your Body Shape
27.content: Understanding whether you're an apple, pear, hourglass, or rectangle helps you choose cuts that enhance your natural proportions rather than fighting them.

28.title: Match Your Metals
28.content: Keep your jewellery and hardware (belt buckles, bag clasps, shoe details) in the same metal family for a cohesive, polished look.

29.title: Bags Should Suit Your Frame
29.content: Choose bag sizes proportional to your body - petite frames suit smaller bags, while taller frames can carry larger styles without being overwhelmed.

30.title: Watches as Statement Pieces
30.content: A quality watch is both functional and fashionable. Choose a style that reflects your personality - classic, sporty, or minimalist - and wear it daily.

31.title: Scarves Transform Outfits
31.content: A silk scarf can be worn around the neck, as a headband, tied to a bag, or as a belt. This versatile accessory elevates simple outfits instantly.

32.title: Belt Placement Matters
32.content: Wear belts at your natural waist for the most flattering effect. Low-slung belts can shorten your torso while high belts elongate legs.

33.title: Sunglasses Shape Your Face
33.content: Choose sunglasses that contrast with your face shape - round faces suit angular frames, square faces look great in rounded styles.

34.title: Less is More with Jewellery
34.content: Choose one focal point - statement earrings OR a bold necklace OR stacked bracelets. Wearing everything at once dilutes impact.

35.title: Match Bag and Shoes Loosely
35.content: Perfectly matching bags and shoes looks dated. Instead, aim for complementary colours or one shared element (both leather, both metallic hardware).

36.title: Hats Complete Outfits
36.content: The right hat adds personality and polish. Choose styles that suit your face shape and lifestyle - from fedoras to baseball caps to berets.

37.title: Invest in Quality Leather Goods
37.content: A well-made leather bag and belt last decades and develop beautiful patina. Choose classic shapes in versatile colours for maximum wearability.

38.title: Layered Necklaces
38.content: Layer necklaces in varying lengths (choker, princess, opera) for modern dimension. Keep metals consistent and vary chain textures and pendant sizes.

39.title: Earrings Frame Your Face
39.content: Earrings draw attention to your face. Choose styles that complement your face shape - studs for everyday, drops for evening, hoops for versatility.

40.title: Texture Mixing
40.content: Combine different textures (silk with denim, cashmere with leather, linen with wool) to add depth and visual interest to monochromatic or simple outfits.

41.title: Natural Fibres Breathe Better
41.content: Cotton, linen, wool, and silk regulate temperature better than synthetics. Prioritise natural fabrics for comfort and longevity.

42.title: Knit for Comfort, Woven for Structure
42.content: Knit fabrics (jersey, ponte) offer stretch and comfort. Woven fabrics (cotton poplin, denim) provide structure. Choose based on desired effect.

43.title: Silk for Special Occasions
43.content: Silk adds instant luxury and elegance. Reserve it for occasions when you want to feel special - the weight and drape are unmatched.

44.title: Cashmere is Worth It
44.content: Quality cashmere is soft, warm, and lightweight. Invest in classic pieces that you'll wear for years - the cost per wear makes it worthwhile.

45.title: Denim Versatility
45.content: Quality denim is the backbone of casual style. Own at least one pair of well-fitting jeans and a denim jacket - both work across seasons and occasions.

46.title: Linen Embraces Wrinkles
46.content: Linen is meant to wrinkle - it's part of its relaxed charm. Embrace the natural creasing rather than fighting it. Reserve for casual settings.

47.title: Velvet for Drama
47.content: Velvet catches light beautifully and adds instant drama to any outfit. Reserve for evening, autumn/winter, or when you want to make an entrance.

48.title: Leather as a Statement
48.content: Leather (or quality vegan alternatives) adds edge and structure. A leather jacket is a wardrobe staple that works across seasons and styles.

49.title: Sheer Fabric Layering
49.content: Sheer fabrics add dimension when layered properly. Always consider what's visible underneath - use intentional layering pieces for polished looks.

50.title: Dress for the Occasion Plus One
50.content: Aim to be slightly better dressed than the occasion requires. Being underdressed feels awkward, while being slightly overdressed signals effort and respect.

51.title: Understand Dress Codes
51.content: From black-tie to smart casual, understanding dress codes prevents embarrassment. When in doubt, ask the host or err on the side of formality.

52.title: Workwear Foundations
52.content: Build a work wardrobe of interchangeable pieces: blazers, tailored trousers, quality blouses, and modest dresses. Aim for one week's worth of outfits.

53.title: Weekend Casual vs Sloppy
53.content: Casual doesn't mean careless. Well-fitting jeans, clean trainers, and a quality t-shirt look effortlessly stylish. Stains and rips look sloppy.

54.title: Date Night Effort
54.content: Dressing up for dates shows effort and respect. Choose pieces that make you feel confident and attractive - your energy will shine through.

55.title: Travel in Comfort and Style
55.content: Airport style should prioritise comfort without sacrificing polish. Stretchy fabrics, slip-on shoes, and layers handle temperature changes and long journeys.

56.title: Interview Impressions
56.content: First impressions matter in interviews. Research the company culture and dress one level more formal than daily wear. Avoid distracting patterns or accessories.

57.title: Wedding Guest Etiquette
57.content: Never wear white to a wedding (unless specifically requested). Match formality to the venue and time. When in doubt, cocktail attire is safe.

58.title: Funeral Respect
58.content: Funerals call for dark, conservative clothing. Black, navy, or charcoal in simple, modest cuts show respect. Save bright colours for celebrations of life.

59.title: Cultural Context Matters
59.content: Research dress expectations when visiting different cultures or religious sites. Modesty requirements, head coverings, or shoe removal may apply.

60.title: Invest in Quality Basics
60.content: Build your wardrobe foundation with well-made basics: a white shirt, dark trousers, quality denim, and a versatile blazer. Quality over quantity always wins.

61.title: The Power of Tailoring
61.content: Well-fitted clothes look more expensive than ill-fitting designer pieces. Invest in alterations for key pieces - the difference is transformative.

62.title: The 80/20 Wardrobe Rule
62.content: You wear 20% of your wardrobe 80% of the time. Identify those key pieces and invest in their quality. Audit and edit your wardrobe regularly.

63.title: Cost Per Wear Calculation
63.content: Divide the price by expected wears. A £200 coat worn 100 times costs £2 per wear - better value than a £50 coat worn 10 times.

64.title: Classic Over Trendy
64.content: Invest in timeless pieces and save trends for inexpensive accessories. A classic trench outlasts a trendy silhouette by decades.

65.title: Quality Shoes Matter Most
65.content: People notice shoes. Invest in well-made, classic styles that can be resoled. Your feet will thank you and your outfits will look elevated.

66.title: The Perfect White Shirt
66.content: Every wardrobe needs a crisp white shirt. Look for quality cotton, proper fit through the shoulders, and a collar that lies flat.

67.title: Investment Outerwear
67.content: Coats are visible and make first impressions. Invest in quality outerwear in versatile colours - they frame your entire look.

68.title: Build Slowly and Thoughtfully
68.content: A curated wardrobe takes time. Add pieces gradually, ensuring each one works with what you already own. Resist impulse purchases.

69.title: Know Your Non-Negotiables
69.content: Identify which items you refuse to compromise on (comfort, ethical production, specific brands) and prioritise spending there.

70.title: Care for Your Clothes
70.content: Read care labels, use proper hangers, and store items correctly. Well-maintained clothes last longer and look better with every wear.

71.title: Wash Less, Air More
71.content: Most clothes don't need washing after every wear. Airing garments between wears extends their life and reduces environmental impact.

72.title: Proper Hanger Selection
72.content: Use wooden or padded hangers for structured items, velvet for slippery fabrics, and fold knits to prevent shoulder bumps.

73.title: Shoe Care Routine
73.content: Clean, condition, and protect shoes regularly. Use shoe trees to maintain shape. Rotate pairs to allow them to dry between wears.

74.title: Repair Before Replace
74.content: A loose button, small hole, or broken zip can often be repaired cheaply. Extend garment life through prompt repairs rather than replacing.

75.title: Seasonal Storage
75.content: Clean items before storing, use breathable garment bags, and add cedar or lavender for moth prevention. Proper storage preserves quality.

76.title: Pilling Prevention
76.content: Pill removal tools restore knits to near-new condition. Prevent pilling by washing inside-out, using gentle cycles, and avoiding friction.

77.title: Stain Treatment Basics
77.content: Treat stains immediately, working from outside in. Know which treatments work for which stains - cold water for blood, club soda for wine.

78.title: Professional Care When Needed
78.content: Some items require professional cleaning. Suits, silk, leather, and heavily beaded pieces should go to trusted dry cleaners or specialists.

79.title: Iron and Steam Properly
79.content: Different fabrics need different heat settings. Always iron inside-out for delicates, use pressing cloths, and steam to refresh between washes.

80.title: Seasonal Fabric Choices
80.content: Match fabric weights to seasons: linen and cotton for summer, wool and cashmere for winter. This keeps you comfortable and appropriately dressed.

81.title: Layering for Transitional Weather
81.content: Spring and autumn require versatile layering. Build outfits that can adapt to temperature changes throughout the day.

82.title: Summer Heat Strategies
82.content: Light colours reflect heat, loose fits allow airflow, and natural fibres breathe. Dress strategically for summer comfort and style.

83.title: Winter Warmth Layers
83.content: Layer for winter warmth: moisture-wicking base, insulating middle, weather-resistant outer. This system keeps you warm without bulk.

84.title: Transitional Wardrobe Pieces
84.content: Trench coats, lightweight knits, and versatile blazers work across seasons. Invest in pieces that bridge weather transitions.

85.title: Weather-Appropriate Footwear
85.content: Match shoes to conditions: water-resistant for rain, insulated for cold, breathable for heat. Style and function can coexist.

86.title: Colour Palette by Season
86.content: Shift your colour palette with seasons: earthy tones for autumn, cool neutrals for winter, soft pastels for spring, vibrant brights for summer.

87.title: Holiday Dressing
87.content: Build a small collection of festive pieces that work across holiday occasions. Metallics, velvet, and jewel tones suit most celebrations.

88.title: Outdoor Event Preparation
88.content: For outdoor events, prepare for weather changes: bring layers, waterproofs, or sun protection as needed. Check the forecast and venue.

89.title: Seasonal Wardrobe Rotation
89.content: Rotate your wardrobe seasonally. Store off-season items properly and bring out fresh pieces - it keeps your closet manageable and inspiring.

90.title: Confidence is Your Best Accessory
90.content: Wear what makes you feel confident and comfortable. The best-dressed people own their personal style rather than following every trend.

91.title: Dress for Now, Not Later
91.content: Don't wait until you lose weight or reach a goal. Dress beautifully for the body you have today - you deserve to feel good now.

92.title: Ignore Size Labels
92.content: Sizes vary wildly between brands. Focus on fit, not the number on the label. The best-fitting size is the right size.

93.title: Highlight What You Love
93.content: Instead of hiding perceived flaws, draw attention to features you love. Great arms? Show them. Love your legs? Wear shorter hemlines.

94.title: Comfort Breeds Confidence
94.content: When you're constantly adjusting or uncomfortable, it shows. Prioritise clothes that fit well and feel good - your confidence will follow.

95.title: Personal Style Over Fashion Rules
95.content: Style rules are guidelines, not laws. If a 'rule' doesn't work for you or make you happy, break it. Authentic personal style trumps all.

96.title: Embrace Your Unique Features
96.content: What makes you different makes you memorable. Embrace unique features - unusual proportions, distinctive colouring, or atypical shapes can become signature style elements.

97.title: Age Appropriateness is a Myth
97.content: There's no age limit on style. Wear what makes you feel wonderful, whether that's mini skirts at 60 or sophisticated suits at 25.

98.title: Quality Over Quantity
98.content: Invest in fewer, better pieces rather than fast fashion. Quality fabrics, construction, and timeless design outlast trends and cost less per wear.

99.title: Secondhand First
99.content: Before buying new, check secondhand options. Charity shops, vintage stores, and resale platforms offer unique pieces with lower environmental impact.

100.title: Know Your Brands
100.content: Research the ethics and sustainability practices of brands you buy from. Support those aligned with your values for production, workers, and environment.

101.title: The One In, One Out Rule
101.content: For every new item added to your wardrobe, donate or sell one. This maintains a manageable wardrobe and encourages thoughtful purchasing.

102.title: Capsule Wardrobe Mindset
102.content: A capsule wardrobe of 30-40 versatile pieces that all work together reduces decision fatigue and environmental impact while maximising style.

103.title: Repair and Upcycle
103.content: Learn basic repairs or find a good tailor. Breathe new life into old pieces through alterations, dyeing, or creative reimagining.

104.title: Rent for Special Occasions
104.content: For one-time events, consider rental services. Access designer pieces without the cost or environmental impact of single-use purchases.

105.title: Natural Fibre Priority
105.content: Choose natural, biodegradable fibres (cotton, linen, wool, silk) over synthetics when possible. They're better for the planet and often more comfortable.
